title: Kant
note: Kant argued that the mind supplies the forms of experience: space, time, and concepts like cause. So we can know some things a priori about appearances, but not things as they are in themselves. In ethics, the moral law is a categorical imperative that reason gives itself, binding all rational beings regardless of their desires.

read.title: The mind's contribution
text: Hume had shown that experience never reveals necessary connection, yet mathematics and physics seem to give necessary truths about the world. Kant proposed a reversal. Instead of assuming our knowledge must conform to objects, suppose objects as we experience them must conform to the structure of our minds. Space and time are the forms of all our sensing, and concepts like substance and cause are the rules by which understanding organizes what we sense. Because we supply these forms, we can know a priori that every experienced event has a cause.

The price is a limit. We know things as they appear to us, phenomena, not as they are in themselves. When reason tries to go beyond possible experience, to prove or disprove God, freedom, or the soul's immortality, it reaches no knowledge. Kant said he had to deny knowledge to make room for faith.

In ethics, Kant held that the moral law does not depend on our desires. Its command is categorical: act only on a maxim you could will as a universal law. The same law demands that we treat every person always as an end, never merely as a means, because rational beings have dignity, not a price.
